correctness.rationale: The synchronous count transition on K_{a,b} is exactly a pair of independent conditional binomial kernels, with strict opposite-side majority giving all 0/all 1 and tie giving a binomial draw. At even times, each side depends on its own initial fixed state and disjoint alternating sets of tie coins; their eventual monochrome colors are independent. A tied U side restarts after two rounds with probability BD and has blue limit u*=(C+DA)/(1−BD); similarly v*=(A+BC)/(1−BD), where A,B use Bin(a,p_U) and C,D Bin(b,p_V). Since B,D<=1/2, BD<=1/4, extinction of both tie substates is a.s.; eventual class probabilities are uv,(1−u)(1−v),u(1−v)+(1−u)v. Union-geometric bound yields E[T]<=22/3; binomial CLT at p=1/2+lambda/sqrt(N) proves the claimed critical normal profile, provided both side sizes are even, initially tied, and a/N has interior limit. Independently solved an 11-transient-state small exact absorbing chain; no extrapolation from its finite size.
residual_risks: Uniform 22/3 is an upper bound, not an equality or best constant.
Sidewise fixed biases and independent tie randomness are essential; updates are synchronous, neighbors only.
